name: Rani-ki-Vav (the Queen’s Stepwell) at Patan, Gujarat
description: Rani-ki-Vav is an 11th-century stepwell in Patan, Gujarat, built beside the Saraswati River as a memorial to a king and designed like a temple turned upside down. Visitors descend seven levels of stairs lined with carved panels, more than 500 major sculptures of gods, mythic scenes and daily life, until they reach a deep water tank 23 metres below ground.
